routes.reason: MixedHodgeModulesAndIrregularHodgeTheory (new, 25 items) — Accept, and the `new` claim is justified — the strongest claim a route can make, so I checked it hardest. **No roadmap in the atlas covers this ground**: of the 211 roadmaps, none has 'mixed Hodge module', 'irregular Hodge', 'exponential motive' or 'twistor' in its title or summary, and the only titles sharing vocabulary are p-adic Hodge theory roadmaps (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory, PadicHodgeTheory, PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology), which are a different subject. No other paper proposes a competing identity for it either: the only nearby `new` proposals in the corpus are PadicHodgeParametersInLocallyAnalyticRepresentations (DING-25), AdmissiblePairsAndPadicHodgeStructures (HOWE-KLEVDAL-26) and HodgeClassesForJacquetLanglands (ICHINO-PRASANNA-23), all p-adic or Hodge-cycle roadmaps. The 25 items are the appendix's material — mixed Hodge modules, the exponential mixed Hodge structures of §A, the irregular Hodge filtration — which is exactly a missing foundation rather than a Part II of anything present.

KloostermanMomentsAndPotentialAutomorphy (new, 46 items) — Accept, and it is already a joined identity: **PAPER-XU-ZHU-22 ('Bessel F-isocrystals for reductive groups') routes 3 items to this same roadmap**, citing this extraction by name — 'PAPER-FRESAN-SABBAH-YU-22 proposed KloostermanMomentsAndPotentialAutomorphy, whose brief plans Deligne's Kloosterman sheaf with its local invariants, the Kloosterman connection Kl_{n+1} ... and Katz's monodromy groups'. So this paper is the originator and the proposal has already been adopted downstream, which is the best evidence that the identity is the right one. The two atlas roadmaps sharing vocabulary — PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems and PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure — are about the automorphy machinery this roadmap would *use*, not about Kloosterman sums, and the extraction routes its automorphy inputs to ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions separately.

ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions (source, 2 items) — Accept. ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions:ML.2 exists in the atlas and owns the modularity/automorphy input the two items take as given, which is the right division: this paper proves the Hodge and L-function statements and imports the automorphy.

PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology (source, 5 items) — Accept. RD.6 and RD.7 both exist and own the rigid-cohomology and p-adic differential-equation material of §5's local computations, which the paper uses rather than develops.
LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles (source, 2 items) — Accept. LPV.2 exists and owns the Picard–Lefschetz input for ordinary quadratic points that the two items (one of them planned item 77) need.
ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations (source, 2 items) — Accept. R01.2 exists and owns Weil–Deligne representations and local epsilon-factors, which §5.2 imports for the functional equation.
